headline: IonQ, a maker of quantum computers, has agreed to buy the network-security company Elisity in a stock deal worth up to $1.3 billion.
score_reason: Pool score 6, lowered by 1 because the deal was announced on 12 Oct 2026, before the 13 Oct window; the facts match the headline.
importance_line: Hospitals, health care companies and other buyers of Elisity's security software would get a quantum-focused owner, but the stated link between this software and quantum threats is IonQ's own argument and the deal still needs regulatory approval and has not closed.
summary: IonQ, which builds trapped-ion quantum computers, announced on 12 Oct 2026 that it has agreed to acquire Elisity, a company whose software stops attackers from spreading through an organisation's network, in an all-stock deal worth up to $1.3 billion, of which up to $150 million depends on Elisity's future performance. IonQ chief executive Niccolo de Masi told The Wall Street Journal, as relayed by The Quantum Insider, that companies and the US government must prepare for the day quantum computers can break today's encryption; closing is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to regulatory approval.
notes: Pool item came from SC Media (blocked); IonQ's own release is the original and is linked. Category kept RES (default); it could also sit in MKT as a deal. Lowered 1 point as the announcement was on 12 Oct 2026.
